question: Is snapshot-fork continuation plus explicit-confirmation archive an acceptable phase-one boundary when Codex activity outside this App Server remains process-local and cannot be fenced?
rationale: The patch can verify its own App Server state and OpenClaw-owned descendants, but accepting possible independent native-runner activity is a product and security policy choice rather than a mechanically provable code property.

options.title: Accept the phase-one boundary
options.body: Land after real native proof confirms snapshot-fork continuation, model locking, and the documented confirmation-gated archive behavior.

options.title: Defer native archive
options.body: Ship discovery and model-locked continuation but remove archive until a lease or stronger cross-process ownership signal exists.

options.title: Keep supervision read-only
options.body: Defer all mutation controls until exact source-thread ownership can be established.

recommendation.title: Accept the phase-one boundary
recommendation.body: Land after real native proof confirms snapshot-fork continuation, model locking, and the documented confirmation-gated archive behavior.
